16ba4963e656.text_content: "RAINBOW" REGISTERED FOR USE ON ALL STANDARD AND NOISELESS TYPEWRITERS CARBON PAPER Writing Strength Chart In both Carbons and Ribbons No. 40 means Medium Writing Strength. Lower numbers indicate a sharper or lighter write—while higher numbers indicate a stronger or darker write. No. 34 Means Sharp, or Light Writing Strength No. 37 " Medium-Sharp " No. 40 " Medium " No. 43 " Medium-Intense " No. 46 " Intense or Strong " IMPORTANT—These numbers are merely descriptive of the approximate writing strength of the carbon paper. While some brands are made in more than our writing strength, the numbers in no way imply that a given carbon is made in any other writing strength than that marked on the end label of the box. The numeral preceding the writing strength number indicates the weight of paper. For example: SILK GAUZE 5-46 means a 5 lb. Sheet of Dark Writing Strength. CLASSIC 7-40 means a 7 lb. or Standard Weight Paper of Medium Write. IMPORTANT—In general, Light Weights and Intense Writing Strengths make better Manifolding Carbons. Lighter Writing Strengths are Cleaner Carbons. Heavy Weights are more durable, and Intense Write is less inclined to Curl. In all instances, the touch of the operator, the condition of the typewriter, and the quality of the copy paper in use are strong factors in obtaining desired results. RAINBOW is made in 7, 5 and 4 lb. weights and in Nos. 46 and 40 Writing Strengths only. GLEN COVE NY
